To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human bone-metastaic prostate tumor cells express E-selectin ligants that are associated with the bone-metastasis of prostate cancer.

E-selectin and its ligands, P- and E-selectin glycoproteins (P- and E-selectins, respectively), are important mediators of prostate tumor metastasis to bone and that P-selectin glyoprotein ligand- 1 and E-selecting ligand-1 are differentially expressed on prostate tumors and may play different roles in prostate tumor metastasis in vivo.

human prostate tumor cell lines derived from bone, brain, and lymph node metastases express the leukocyte E-selectins ligands, PSGL-1, and ESL-1, and that PSGL-1 may contribute to the bone tropism and metastasis of prostate tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of prostate tumor progression and bone tropism.
the identification and characterization of E-selectin-binding glycoproteins on metastatic human prostate tumor cells and their potential roles in the progression and metastasis of prostate cancer.
the identification of the E-selectin ligans, PSGL-1, and ESL-1, on metastatic prostate tumor cell lines and the expression of PSGL- 1 on the surface of bone-metastaic prostate tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of PSGL- and ESL-1 on the surface of prostate tumor cells is associated with bone-malignant progression and metastasis.

ESL-1 is a novel E-selectin liganded protein that is associated with prostate tumor progression, whereas PSGL1 is an E-selectin liganed protein that is associated specifically with prostate tumor bone metastasis.
PSGL-1 is a novel and important determinant of human prostate tumor bone tropism and metastasis, whereas ESL-1 plays a more general and less specific role in prostate tumor progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PSGL-1 is the principal ligand for E-selectin in the metastasis of human prostate tumor cells to bone and ESL-1 is expressed in all stages of prostate tumor progression and may play an important role in the early stages of prostate tumor metastasis.

the expression pattern of ESL-1 is consistent with the metastatic progression of prostate tumor cells, and the expression of PSGL- 1 is associated with the bone-metastasis potential of prostate tumor cells.
the expression of ESL-1 is not associated with bone metastasis in prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
E-selectin is a key player in the bone tropic nature of human prostate tumor cells.
the expression of PSGL- 1 on the surface of prostate tumor cells is associated with the metastatic phenotype.
E-selectin and PSGL-1 are critical for the bone tropism and metastasis of prostate tumor cells.
